name: Wolf
description: Wolf has found $$$n$$$ sheep with tastiness values $$$p_1, p_2, ..., p_n$$$ where $$$p$$$ is a permutation$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$. Wolf wants to perform binary search on $$$p$$$ to find the sheep with tastiness of $$$k$$$, but $$$p$$$ may not necessarily be sorted. The success of binary search on the range $$$[l, r]$$$ for $$$k$$$ is represented as $$$f(l, r, k)$$$, which is defined as follows: If $$$l \gt r$$$, then $$$f(l, r, k)$$$ fails. Otherwise, let $$$m = \lfloor\frac{l + r}{2}\rfloor$$$, and: If $$$p_m = k$$$, then $$$f(l, r, k)$$$ is successful , If $$$p_m \lt k$$$, then $$$f(l, r, k) = f(m+1, r, k)$$$, If $$$p_m \gt k$$$, then $$$f(l, r, k) = f(l, m-1, k)$$$. Cow the Nerd decides to help Wolf out. Cow the Nerd is given $$$q$$$ queries, each consisting of three integers $$$l$$$, $$$r$$$, and $$$k$$$. Before the search begins, Cow the Nerd may choose a non-negative integer $$$d$$$, and $$$d$$$ indices $$$1 \le i_1 \lt i_2 \lt \ldots \lt i_d \le n$$$ where $$$p_{i_j} \neq k$$$ over all $$$1 \leq j \leq d$$$. Then, he may re-order the elements $$$p_{i_1}, p_{i_2}, ..., p_{i_d}$$$ however he likes. For each query, output the minimum integer $$$d$$$ that Cow the Nerd must choose so that $$$f(l, r, k)$$$ can be successful , or report that it is impossible. Note that the queries are independent and the reordering is not actually performed. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A permutation of length $$$n$$$ is an array that contains every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ exactly once.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ $$$(1 \le t \le 10^4)$$$ — the number of test cases. The first line of each test contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ $$$(1 \le n, q \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the length of $$$p$$$ and the number of queries respectively. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, ..., p_n$$$ — the tastiness of the $$$i$$$-th sheep. It is guaranteed that every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ appears exactly once in $$$p$$$. The following $$$q$$$ lines contain three integers $$$l$$$, $$$r$$$, and $$$k$$$ $$$(1 \le l \le r \le n, 1 \le k \le n)$$$ — the range that the binary search will be performed on and the integer being searched for each query. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ and the sum of $$$q$$$ over all cases do not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each query, output the minimum integer $$$d$$$ that Cow the Nerd must choose so that $$$f(l, r, k)$$$ is successful on a new line. If it is impossible, output $$$-1$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2106E — Wolf [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
